cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt. Amos 3:1 says the LORD's word is against the whole family He brought up out of the land of Egypt. He is speaking to the children of Israel, friends.

The answer is that He will punish them for all their iniquities. The LORD says, “Only you have I known from all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities” (Amos 3:2). Notice the word 'therefore.' It ties being known by Him to what comes next. This is a serious line, friends, so I'll let it sit for a second.

The answer is that a lion roars when he has prey. The question is, “Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey?” (Amos 3:4). The answer is built right in. Amos asks it again about a young lion: “Does a young lion growl in his den if he has caught nothing?”

The word is catch, friends. The text asks, “Does a trap spring from the ground when it has nothing to catch?” (Amos 3:5). No catch, no spring. Right before that, a bird doesn't land in a snare where no bait has been set. Amos keeps stacking up these everyday pictures.

The answer is tremble, bakers. Amos asks, “If a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble?” (Amos 3:6). When the horn sounds in a city, the people tremble. The answer is built right into the question.

The answer is True. Amos asks, “If calamity comes to a city, has not the LORD caused it?” (Amos 3:6). The question points to the LORD as the One who caused it. That's the point Amos is making as the questions pile up, friends.

The answer is His servants the prophets. The text says, “Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets” (Amos 3:7). Just after that, the passage says, “The Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?” (Amos 3:8). So the prophets are the ones He shares His plan with, bakers.

The answer is False. Amos says, “The Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?” (Amos 3:8). The verse doesn't say a person could hear Him and stay quiet. It asks who won't prophesy once the Lord GOD has spoken. Worth catching, friends.

The answer is the great unrest and the acts of oppression. Ashdod and Egypt are told to assemble on the mountains of Samaria and see the great unrest in the city and the acts of oppression in her midst (Amos 3:9). They're called to take a look, friends. I think this one hurts.
The answer is False. The LORD declares, “For they know not how to do right…” (Amos 3:10). It's a hard thing to read, friends, and it sets up what comes next.

The answer is violence and destruction. The LORD says, “They store up violence and destruction in their citadels” (Amos 3:10). A citadel is a stronghold, and what they've stored up in theirs is not good. I think this one hurts, friends.

The answer is that an enemy will surround the land. The Lord GOD says, “An enemy will surround the land; he will pull down your strongholds and plunder your citadels” (Amos 3:11). That word 'Therefore' at the start of the verse connects it to what came before. It's a heavy moment, bakers, so I'll keep it simple.

The answer is True. The LORD says the Israelites dwelling in Samaria will be rescued having just the corner of a bed or the cushion of a couch (Amos 3:12). It's like a shepherd snatching two legs or a piece of an ear from a lion's mouth. It's a hard picture, friends, so I'll keep it simple.

The answer is Jacob. The Lord GOD, the God of Hosts, says, “Hear and testify against the house of Jacob…” (Amos 3:13). The One speaking is the Lord GOD Himself, and the house He names is Jacob's, bakers.

The answer is that they'll be cut off and fall to the ground. The LORD says, “the horns of the altar will be cut off, and they will fall to the ground” (Amos 3:14). It's all part of the day He punishes Israel for their transgressions. A very serious day, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will tear down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will also perish, and the great houses will come to an end…” (Amos 3:15). Neither house is left standing, friends. It's a little detail, but it matters.
